transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I know everyone keeps telling me I’m wrong, but I’m absolutely certain about what my husband is hiding from me, and nothing they say changes my mind. It is just so frustrating that nobody will believe me when I know exactly what is going on.
How long have you been absolutely certain about this belief—has it been at least one month, or did it start more recently?

Oh, it's been much longer than just a month. It’s been a little over a year now—since about last spring—that I’ve been completely convinced he's hiding this from me. I just haven’t been able to let it go because I know the truth.
Has this belief caused problems in your daily life, relationships, or work, or is it mainly limited to this one concern?

Apart from this, I still do my housework, go to choir, and run my home-organizing jobs just fine. But it has caused a lot of arguments at home, to the point where my kids visit less because they're tired of hearing about it. I've also started skipping some choir and walking group outings if I think my husband or that woman might be there.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things other people don’t, or felt that others are trying to control, monitor, or send you special messages through TV, radio, or the internet?

Goodness, no, I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there, and the TV isn't sending me messages. I'm not crazy; my only concern is what my husband is hiding from me. Why would you even ask me about things like that?
Have you ever used any drugs, heavy alcohol, or had a medical problem like a brain injury, seizure disorder, or thyroid illness around the time this belief started?

No, I don't use any drugs and I've never been a heavy drinker. I've also never had any medical issues like a brain injury, seizures, or thyroid problems. Physically, my health has always been perfectly fine.
Over the past year, have you had any periods of feeling unusually depressed, very energized, needing much less sleep, or losing interest in things, or has this belief been the only major problem?

No, I haven't had any of those mood swings or trouble sleeping; this belief is really the only major problem. I still manage my housework, choir, and home-organization jobs perfectly fine. It's just the stress from the family arguments and having to skip certain outings to avoid them.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a single, fixed persecutory/jealous-type delusional belief lasting over 1 year, with preserved functioning aside from relationship conflict and avoidance. There are no hallucinations, no prominent mood episode, no substance use, and no medical/neurologic cause identified. The presentation is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder.
